provenance.title: Resurgence of Chern-Simons theory at the trivial flat connection
provenance.authors: STAVROS GAROUFALIDIS, JIE GU, MARCOS MARIÑO, AND CAMPBELL WHEELER

candidates.statement: We should point out that the above series are well-defined (for $\sigma\neq \sigma_0$ via formal Gaussian integration using as input an ideal triangulation of a 3-manifold [@DG], and for $\sigma=\sigma_0$ using the Kashaev invariant itself) and their coefficients are (up to multiplication by a power of $2\pi{\rm i}$) algebraic numbers.

We should point out that although a proof of resurgence of the asymptotic series $\Phi^{(\sigma)}(h)$ is *still* missing, the current paper (as well as the prior ones [@GGM:resurgent; @GGM:peacock]) provide a complete description of their resurgent structure (namely the location of the singularities and a calculation of the Stokes constants) with precise statements, complemented by extensive numerical computations (including a numerical computation of the Stokes constants).

We should point out that the definition of the top row of the $3 \times 3$ matrices for the $\mathbf{4}_1$ knot, and the $6 \times 6$ matrix for the $\mathbf{5}_2$ knot, as well as an extension of the above results to the case of closed hyperbolic 3-manifolds have been taken from the forthcoming thesis of the last author.
candidates.section_title: Illustration with the two simplest hyperbolic knots

candidates.statement: Finally, in order to compute the global Stokes matrix $\mathfrak{S}_{II\rightarrow III}(\tilde{q})$, we need to take into account that the odd powers of $\tau^{1/2}$ on both sides of [\[eq:GMsPhi\]](#eq:GMsPhi){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:GMsPhi"} give rise to additional $-1$ factors when one crosses the branch cut at the negative real axis, and [\[eq:SMM\]](#eq:SMM){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:SMM"} should be modified by $$\mathfrak{S}_{II\rightarrow III}(\tilde{q}) = \mathrm{diag}(1,-1,-1) M_{III}(\tilde{q})^{-1}\cdot M_{II}(\tilde{q}),$$ and we find $$\mathfrak{S}_{II\rightarrow III} = \begin{pmatrix} 1&1&0\\ 0&1&0\\ 0&-3&1 \end{pmatrix}.$$ Similarly this can be identified as $\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$ associated to the ray $\rho_{\pi}$ and it can be factorised as $$\mathfrak{S}_{\pi} = \mathfrak{S}_{\iota_{0,1}}\mathfrak{S}_{\iota_{2,1}},\quad \mathfrak{S}_{\iota_{0,1}} = \begin{pmatrix} 1&1&0\\ 0&1&0\\ 0&0&1 \end{pmatrix},\quad \mathfrak{S}_{\iota_{2,1}} = \begin{pmatrix} 1&0&0\\ 0&1&0\\ 0&-3&1 \end{pmatrix}.$$ Note that the local Stokes matrices $\mathfrak{S}_{\iota_{0,1}}$ and $\mathfrak{S}_{\iota_{2,1}}$ also commute.

Finally, in order to compute the global Stokes matrix $\mathfrak{S}_{II\rightarrow III}(\tilde{q})$, we need to take into account that the odd powers of $\tau^{1/2}$ on both sides of [\[eq:GMsPhi\]](#eq:GMsPhi){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:GMsPhi"} give rise to additional $-1$ factors when one crosses the branch cut at the negative real axis, and [\[eq:SMM\]](#eq:SMM){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:SMM"} should be modified by $$\mathfrak{S}_{II\rightarrow III}(\tilde{q}) = \mathrm{diag}(1,-1,-1) M_{III}(\tilde{q})^{-1}\cdot M_{II}(\tilde{q}),$$ and we find $$\mathfrak{S}_{II\rightarrow III} = \begin{pmatrix} 1&1&0\\ 0&1&0\\ 0&-3&1 \end{pmatrix}.$$ Similarly this can be identified as $\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$ associated to the ray $\rho_{\pi}$ and it can be factorised as $$\mathfrak{S}_{\pi} = \mathfrak{S}_{\iota_{0,1}}\mathfrak{S}_{\iota_{2,1}},\quad \mathfrak{S}_{\iota_{0,1}} = \begin{pmatrix} 1&1&0\\ 0&1&0\\ 0&0&1 \end{pmatrix},\quad \mathfrak{S}_{\iota_{2,1}} = \begin{pmatrix} 1&0&0\\ 0&1&0\\ 0&-3&1 \end{pmatrix}.$$ Note that the local Stokes matrices $\mathfrak{S}_{\iota_{0,1}}$ and $\mathfrak{S}_{\iota_{2,1}}$ also commute.
